itens.t: China launches first international astronaut to Tiangong space station
itens.r: China launched an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station for the first time ever on Tuesday, marking a significant milestone for international participation in the Chinese space program. A Long March rocket lifted off carrying the mission, expanding the station's cooperative framework. Observers noted that this step enhances Beijing's diplomatic footprint in orbital exploration. The historic docking broadens scientific collaboration beyond traditional partnerships.
itens.d:
China launched its first international astronaut to the Tiangong space station on November 24, marking a significant milestone for the country's space program. A Long March 2F rocket carried the Shenzhou-24 crew from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center.

The historic flight included Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who became the first person from his country to reach orbit. China and Pakistan had previously signed a spaceflight cooperation agreement in February 2025 to pave the way for this mission.
itens.e:
China launched its first international astronaut to the Tiangong space station on November 24, using a Long March 2F rocket carrying the Shenzhou-24 crew from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. This historic flight included Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces and the first person from his country to reach orbit.

This mission marks a significant milestone for China's space program and builds upon a spaceflight cooperation agreement signed by China and Pakistan in February 2025. This suggests deepening bilateral ties and highlights how international partnerships are increasingly shaping national space endeavors beyond traditional alliances.

One risk is managing the technical and diplomatic complexities of integrating foreign personnel into sovereign space infrastructure. Observers should watch for future joint missions and whether this cooperation expands to include other partner nations within Tiangong's operational framework.

itens.t: First-ever detection of dying star's final nuclear heartbeat
itens.r: Astronomers have recorded the first-ever detection of a dying star's final nuclear heartbeat before its collapse. This unique observation challenges existing models regarding how medium-mass stars exhaust their fuel.

New observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array in Chile have revealed a dying star's final nuclear heartbeat. Researchers captured a physical snapshot of stellar death throes frozen in gas.
